decision.title: The schema document reader and assembly (packet )
decision.summary: One table of schema element roles drives a loop reading schema documents into components, assembly reads each document once with redefine and override applied last, and RESOLVE turns references into indexes.

body.p: . READ and RESOLVE () and sxml_schema's quintet; golden src/xslt_read.c, src/xquery_module.c.

item.p: One table of schema element roles (src/schema_read.c): a role is what an element is where it appears (global or local element, group definition or reference, a facet, ...); its rule lists the unqualified attributes and required ones the schema for schema documents allows, the child slots its children fill in order (a slot: roles, required, repeated, ending the content), and its reader. Attributes of other namespaces than XSD's are allowed (openAttrs), vc: attributes decide conditional inclusion (4.2.2, src-cip). What breaks the schema for schema documents is reported with the role's representation constraint (src-element, src-ct, src-simple-type, ...), or the component's properties constraint where there is none (mg-props-correct, an-props-correct, n-props-correct, as-props-correct, sch-props-correct); equal id values are cvc-id.2.

The walk is a loop over node indexes from the element read to its last descendant; an element's children get their roles when it is read, so an element without one (ignored, misplaced, in an annotation) is skipped with its subtree. Components are added in document order, linked to the parent's component at once; lists (particles, attribute uses, facets, ...) are written in a second pass, once, whole.

As read, for the later stages: a simple type restriction has variety ATOMIC until RESOLVE gives it its base's; the xs:assertion facets of a simpleContent restriction join the type's assertions with its xs:assert children, in document order; defaultOpenContent is applied to complex content when appliesToEmpty or the type has a particle or complexContent (clause 6's emptiness needs COMPLEX_TYPES); an attribute use with ref and inheritable="false" takes the declaration's.

Assembly (src/schema_assemble.c): a work list; a document is read once by absolute URI and the namespace its components get (a chameleon document included into two namespaces is read twice from one tree); the children of xs:redefine and xs:override are read after every document, replacing the name index entry of what they name (4.2.4, 4.2.5); an override child with nothing to replace is not read; a component replaced twice is src-redefine or src-override; a redefined document that reaches the redefining one is src-redefine; a redefinition's base or self-reference names the original (src-redefine.5, 6.1, 7.1; the original must be the redefined document's). Redefines and overrides are read innermost first (a chain replaces the inner redefinition) and a component replaced twice in one document is the error. A document the resolver does not deliver is no error (4.2.3 clause 2.4, 4.2.6.2; schema.h says otherwise, Proposed); an unlocated import of the xml: namespace reads its known document (xml.xsd); an import without a location of a namespace already read reads nothing; an xs:schema element that conditional inclusion ignores is empty.

Not done: src-redefine 6.2.2 and 7.2.2 (a group or attribute group redefined without a self-reference must restrict the original); the original of an override or redefinition stays a component (unnamed) and is compiled.

RESOLVE (src/schema_resolve.c): references through the name index (src-resolve; src-resolve.4.2 for namespaces not imported, at READ), base, item and member types, restriction varieties, substitution group affiliations, element types through heads, members transitively, ref identity constraints; cycles of groups (mg-props-correct.2), derivations (ct-props-correct.3, st-props-correct.2) and substitution groups (e-props-correct.6), each a walk with an explicit stack. Attribute groups may refer to each other in a cycle (XSD 1.1, bug 15795).
Text form (src/schema_text.c): 's lines for every table, the xs:schema element's namespace context always first, content models (5.6's writer) after the components.
Driver: sxml-xsd-test compiles every schema test and every instance test's schema (resolver over the suite files); instance tests are not run until 5.7 ("XSD validation not implemented").

Measured at 21c9531 with 5.5 and 5.6: schema tests 15,163 of 15,329 in scope pass (98.9 %, gate of the packet 85 %); every schema document reads without a crash, leak or limit (10 particle tests reach the content model state limit in COMPLEX_TYPES); no reader error on a valid schema; the XSD slice 110 of 147.
